transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Mbeki, thank you for coming in to see me today. I have some information regarding your biopsy results that we need to discuss.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've been waiting all week. Just tell me. Is it cancer or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry, but there has been a mistake with your results. The diagnosis of cancer we discussed previously was incorrect.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean incorrect? You told me I had a malignancy. You told me I needed to start preparing for treatment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is shocking. I want to apologize on behalf of our team. We failed you in the process of handling your specimen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Failed me? How do you fail at a biopsy? Did you lose it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the pathology lab with the labels. Basically, the samples got mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mixed up? Are you telling me you gave me someone else's diagnosis?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the labeling system, and the report you received belonged to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I have spent the last three days telling my family I'm sick. I've been calculating how much time I can take off from my business. I can't afford to miss work for some "confusion" in your lab!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are incredibly angry, and you have every right to be.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Angry? I'm terrified! I thought I was dying, and now you're telling me it was a clerical error? Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are responsible. It was our mistake in the lab, and I am truly sorry for the distress this has caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Do I actually have cancer or not? You’re being vague. What exactly happened to my actual piece of tissue?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into the records. There was a discrepancy with the vials.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't answer my question. Do I have cancer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't have the corrected result in front of me yet.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You called me in here to tell me the first result was wrong, but you can't even tell me if I'm actually sick? This is a joke. This is a complete joke.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? My life has been turned upside down for seventy-two hours! My business is running on a skeleton crew because I thought I had to start chemotherapy!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize how much this impacts your work and your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want names. I want to know who swapped the labels.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't provide individual names, but the department is reviewing the incident.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about a review. I want my real results. Now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am working to get those. I’ve put in an urgent request to pathology.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long is an urgent request? Another week? Another month?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I expect to have an answer by tomorrow afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what happens if the second one is wrong too? How can I trust a single word coming out of this clinic?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know the trust is broken right now. We are doing everything to verify the new results personally.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're just saying that. You're just saying words.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. I know an apology doesn't fix the time you've lost.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It doesn't. My business doesn't run on apologies.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call you personally tomorrow by four o'clock with the corrected report.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You'll call me? I shouldn't have to wait for a phone call. I should be getting a written guarantee that this won't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure the final report is sent to your portal and printed for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If this is a mistake, then why did it happen? Why is your lab so incompetent?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a problem with the way the labels were processed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an explanation. That's a hedge.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in our internal protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I actually can't believe this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to go back to my shop. I can't sit here and wait for you to figure out which patient I am.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I will have the answer for you tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow. Four o'clock. If I don't hear from you, I'm calling my lawyer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call you. I'll make sure of it.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the encounter.

A.justification: Direct apologies are used, the team is named as responsible, and accountability is maintained despite the patient's anger.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('angry', 'frustrating') and references specific content the patient shared regarding their business and family.

T.justification: A specific next step and timeline are provided (call by 4pm tomorrow), but there is no named patient role or address of prevention.
